prompt: Research how the write-lock mechanism works across the different IDE adapters (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex). I need to understand: does the write-lock actually fire in all IDEs? What are the behavioral differences? I'm considering whether to add a new IDE adapter and need to know the common contract.

assertions.name: covers-all-three-ides
assertions.description: Output discusses write-lock behavior for all 3 IDEs: Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex

assertions.name: evidence-markers-present
assertions.description: Uses evidence markers (verified/unverified or equivalent) on material claims, not just stating conclusions

assertions.name: behavioral-differences-identified
assertions.description: Identifies at least 2 concrete behavioral differences between IDE adapters (e.g., event types, hook mechanisms, fallback behavior)

assertions.name: actionable-for-new-adapter
assertions.description: Conclusions include guidance actionable for someone building a new IDE adapter (common contract, minimum requirements)

assertions.name: evidence-specificity
assertions.description: Evidence citations reference specific files and line numbers, not just 'I checked the code'
